_: Exceptions manifest for the spec-citation gate (issue #934). See scripts/spec-citations-gate.mjs.
_shrinks: Every entry records a defect someone must fix. Fixing one DELETES its entry — entries are never re-fingerprinted, so this file trends toward empty and the gate's UNRESOLVED counter is a live audit signal rather than a permanent excuse list. The citation entries wait on the sweep in #948, which is deliberately held until spec/ freezes; if that trigger slips, this manifest stops shrinking, and that is the number to watch. One entry is permanent by design: an Accepted ADR is immutable, so a status claim inside one cannot be edited to name an issue.
_fingerprint: An entry is keyed by a hash of the citing line, the citation or claim it excuses, its own why prose, and the issue it is tracked by. Editing any of the four makes the entry stale, so an exception cannot drift away from the text it describes, a rationale cannot be quietly rewritten, and an entry cannot be silently retargeted at a different issue. The observed state and the kind are compared directly rather than hashed, so an entry authored wrong from the start is caught too, not only one edited afterwards. No gate can decide whether a rationale is TRUE; this one guarantees it cannot change unseen.
_coverage: The gate covers a citation that does not RESOLVE, the mechanically checkable half of the wrong-passage mode (a quoted EBNF production absent from the range cited), and a forward-looking status claim naming no tracking issue. It does NOT cover a citation that resolves to the wrong passage while paraphrasing rather than quoting, nor prose beside a correct line that misstates it. Do not read a green run as 'every citation is right'.
